about.title: Personal Injury Help in Menlo Park, California
about.longDescription: Menlo Park may be a small city of just under 34,000 people, but its roads see a steady flow of traffic accidents. In the most recent year of public-record data, the city logged 203 injury collisions and 273 people injured. Corridors like US-101, Willow Road, El Camino Real, and Marsh Road see the highest volume of reported crashes, and Wednesday mornings between 8 and 10 a.m. tend to show more reported incidents than other times. Getting hurt in any of these situations can leave you juggling medical appointments, missed paychecks, and a stack of paperwork you never wanted. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in Menlo Park with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money on your behalf. You don't have to sort through California's legal deadlines and fault rules by yourself. A short conversation with an attorney can help you understand your options before time limits become a problem.

whyChoose.title: Why Menlo Park Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Don't Wait
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Reaching out early helps preserve evidence and options.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning that even if you're partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on What You Can Recover for Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Ordinary injury cases in California don't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your compensation isn't artificially capped by a fixed number.

items.title: No Fee Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means you pay nothing upfront, and legal fees only come out of money actually recovered for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Menlo Park?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government entity was involved — such as a city vehicle or a road maintenance issue — the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Menlo Park?
items.answer: Based on public-record collision counts, corridors including US-101, Willow Road, El Camino Real, and Marsh Road show the highest volume of reported crashes in Menlo Park, with Wednesday mornings between 8 and 10 a.m. showing a noticeable concentration of reports. These are neutral counts, not a judgment about any particular road or intersection.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm. We simply help connect injured people with an independent attorney who can evaluate their situation.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary personal injury cases in California, there's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you.
